analysis: Examined EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (base and head) and EngineV2Factory+Production.swift (patch and base). The PR adds a resolved prefill geometry. It refactors the dense-Qwen3.5 check into isDenseQwen35 and adds isGemma4. Gemma 4 now defaults to a 2048-token plain chunk (usesWidePrefillChunk) and is raised to at least 1120 tokens to cover a media block. New env knobs DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS (lines 66-67, 128-155) are read by productionSchedulerConfig via prefillGeometry. ProductionBuild gains an optional prefillGeometry field, filled from the final schedulerConfig (Production.swift patch, around line 401). The field is read-only telemetry metadata and carries no secrets. Security-relevant behavior: the new env overrides are operator-controlled. The operator is already the adversary for their own machine's availability (ADV-001, TB-003), so they add no new cross-tenant or consumer-reachable attack surface. Nemotron calibrated limits still clamp the chunk after the geometry is resolved (head lines 180-187). GLM scheduler policy overwrites the chunk and step values and disables stripes. Integer overflow in stepTokenBudget is handled with multipliedReportingOverflow. An explicit chunk is not bounded for other families, so memory pressure is possible. That is operator self-DoS and is bounded by the existing KV and activation admission, which are outside the supplied evidence. No change touches the prefix cache (T-041), encryption, attestation, authorization, the coordinator wire contract or key handling. Remaining unverified items for integration: whether the paged pool sizing and activation-reserve floors in unchanged code (prepareProductionBackend, PagedSequenceKV preconditions) hold with the wider Gemma 4 chunk. These are memory and availability concerns, not confidentiality or authorization concerns.
